title: Europa Nostra joins 200+ organisations in calling on EU Member States to reverse the proposed cuts to Creative Europe’s 2027 budget
content:
Europa Nostra has joined more than 200 cultural organisations across Europe in calling on EU Member States to reverse the proposed cuts to Creative Europe’s 2027 budget. The open letter, initiated and coordinated by Culture Action Europe, responds to the Council’s suggestion to reduce the funding the Creative Europe Programme can commit to projects in 2027 by €31.6 million.

The cuts would affect every strand:
– €7.8 million from Culture
– €23.2 million from MEDIA
– €0.6 million from the Cross-sectoral strand

Education, Youth, Culture and Sport Council Meeting, 11-12 May 2026, Brussels. Copyright: European Union

This is the fourth budget year in the current seven-year cycle in which the Council has proposed cuts to Creative Europe, and they are at odds with the EU’s own commitments. In June 2026, the Presidents of the Council, the Parliament and the Commission signed the Joint Declaration “Europe for Culture – Culture for Europe”, committing to ensuring the independence of cultural institutions, artistic freedom and the sustainability of the cultural and creative sectors. The 2027 budget is an immediate opportunity to put those commitments into practice.

title: The Buzludzha Monument, Bulgaria: How to transform contested heritage into a place for dialogue, education and culture
content:
Built in 1981 as the House-Monument of the Bulgarian Communist Party, the Buzludzha Monument in the mountains of central Bulgaria is one of the most striking examples of 20th-century architecture in the country. Following the end of the Communist regime in 1989, the building was abandoned and has since suffered from theft, vandalism and severe weather conditions. Its windows and roof have been severely damaged, leaving the structure exposed to the elements and putting its remarkable interior mosaics at increasing risk. The Buzludzha Monument was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2018 by Europa Nostra.

Since its involvement in the 7 Most Endangered Programme, the Buzludzha Monument has gained increasing international attention and momentum towards its conservation and sustainable future. The Buzludzha Project Foundation has advocated for its stabilisation, preservation and interpretation, with the ambition of demonstrating how difficult and contested heritage can be responsibly conserved and understood.

title: Montenegro celebrates European Heritage Award for Pacijenca Project – Safeguarding the Dobrota Lace Tradition
content:
On 25 September, the Pacijenca Project – Safeguarding the Dobrota Lace Tradition, a 2026 European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award winner, was celebrated with a moving event at St. Tryphon Cathedral in Kotor, Montenegro. “Pacijenca” is the second Montenegrin project to receive Europe’s top heritage award in nearly 25 years. The ceremony, held as part of the European Heritage Days, brought together national and municipal officials, representatives of cultural institutions, the lace-making community led by Nada Radović, and the wider public.

Led by Museums of Kotor, the Pacijenca Project was awarded in the Education, Training and Skills category for reviving the endangered skill of Dobrota needle lace-making through sustained teaching, public demonstrations and contemporary heritage interpretation. Its name comes from the Italian word for patience, “pazienza”.

title: 19th ECTN Conference for Cultural Tourism in Europe: Skiathos hosts European gathering on the future of sustainable cultural tourism
content:
How can tourism help places become more resilient, inclusive and sustainable while strengthening cultural heritage and local communities? This question was at the heart of the 19th ECTN Conference for Cultural Tourism in Europe, held in Skiathos, Greece, from 23 to 26 September 2026, under the theme “Sustainable Tourism Strategy and Culture Compass for Europe: Synergies for Regenerative, Smart and Resilient Cultural Tourism”.

The conference brought together tourism professionals, heritage practitioners, researchers, policymakers and cultural organisations from across Europe to explore the latest developments in cultural, heritage, smart and sustainable tourism. Discussions focused on the role of culture and heritage, digitalisation, climate resilience, regeneration and sustainability in enhancing visitor experiences and supporting more resilient destinations.

title: A gradual path to recovery: How the Polirone Monastic Complex of San Benedetto Po in Italy became a model for community-led conservation
content:
When an earthquake struck the Northern Italian regions of Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy in 2012, the Polirone Monastic Complex of San Benedetto Po suffered extensive damage. The loss was twofold: an impressive 16th-century Renaissance architectural structure was devastated, and its surrounding community lost access to one of their most important cultural spaces.

Since being listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2013, the restoration and recovery of the monastery has become an example of heritage restoration, community in action and resilience, recognised with both a European Heritage Award / Europa Nostra Award and a Grand Prix 2026 in the category Conservation and Adaptive Reuse.

For this Impact Story, Europa Nostra sat down with Federica Guidetti, Curator of Polironiano Civic Museum, who was involved in the nomination of the site for the 7 Most Endangered Programme, to learn more about how this community raised a monastery from the rubble.

title: Inclusive European Heritage Residency 2026 in Malta: peer learning in practice
content:
From 13 to 19 September, Malta’s rich cultural heritage took centre stage during the second Inclusive European Heritage Residency, bringing together 10 selected participants from across Europe for peer learning activities and exchanges with dozens of volunteers and professionals from Din l-Art Helwa – the National Trust for Malta, as well as professionals from Europa Nostra and INTO.

The Residency aimed to strengthen the capacity and connections of heritage organisations across Europe, supporting more inclusive, sustainable and community-led approaches to heritage protection. The Residency was organised in the framework of the network project Europa Nostra Heritage Agora, co-funded by the Creative Europe Programme of the European Union.

title: European experts call for immediate Grade 1 protection and adaptive reuse of British Barracks at Fort Chambray, Malta
content:
A European expert team has released a Report on the preservation of the British Barracks at Fort Chambray in Gozo, Malta. An exceptionally important element of Gozo’s architectural, social and European heritage, the Barracks were constructed at the turn of the 20th century as married quarters for British military families, and are now threatened with demolition to make way for a new five-storey spa hotel, which would incorporate only a reconstructed version of the historic arcaded façade.

The British Barracks at Fort Chambray were listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2026, in the framework of the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra with the support of the European Investment Bank Institute. The site was nominated by Din l-Art Ħelwa – the National Trust for Malta.

The European experts recommend protecting the British Barracks through Grade 1 scheduling and pursuing their adaptive reuse, arguing that conservation and economic development can be mutually supportive and that the building can contribute to the future sustainable development of Fort Chambray and Gozo.

title: Europa Nostra has strategic meeting with Assistant Director-General for Culture at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris
content:
On 16 September 2026, Europa Nostra had an excellent first meeting with Nayef H. Al-fayez, UNESCO Assistant Director-General for Culture, at UNESCO Headquarters in Paris, France. Secretary General Sneška Quaedvlieg-Mihailović and Board Member Laurent Lévi-Strauss, himself a former high-official of UNESCO, represented Europa Nostra at this strategic meeting.

The discussion focused on the centrality of culture and cultural heritage for peace, climate action and the overall resilience of our shared humanity. To champion this strategic goal, we need an even stronger partnership between UNESCO and the European Union, with the vital contribution of civil society.

Credit: Europa Nostra

title: British-Turkish novelist and storyteller Elif Shafak wins Helena Vaz da Silva European Award 2026
content:
Press release English – Portuguese

The acclaimed British-Turkish author Elif Shafak is the winner of the Helena Vaz da Silva European Award for Raising Public Awareness on Cultural Heritage 2026. This European recognition pays tribute to Elif Shafak’s exceptional ability to bring Europe’s rich and diverse cultural heritage to life through her captivating storytelling, while responding to the challenges of our time with a powerful call for defending democracy, promoting solidarity, embracing cosmopolitanism and celebrating cultural diversity.

Elif Shafak – Photo credit: Ferhat Elik

The Helena Vaz da Silva European Award was established in 2013 by the Centro Nacional de Cultura (Portugal) in collaboration with Europa Nostra and the Portuguese Press Club, and has the support of the Ministry of Culture, Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Portugal, the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation and Tourism of Portugal.

The award ceremony will take place on 5 November at the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation in Lisbon, Portugal.
creator: Joana Pinheiro
sourceDescription: The Voice of Cultural Heritage in Europe

title: Cross-border community in action: How the Historic Centre of Stolberg (Germany) came back to life
content:
After a mass flood in mid-July 2021 devastated the Historic Centre of Stolberg in the western part of Germany, causing severe damage to hundreds of buildings, the centre of the 500-year-old town was listed among the 7 Most Endangered heritage sites in Europe for 2022. Since its involvement in the 7 Most Endangered Programme run by Europa Nostra, the Historic Centre of Stolberg  has not only been successfully rebuilt, but strengthened its network and community in the process — a completely unexpected, and very welcome outcome of the selection. Europa Nostra sat down with Dr. Karl Schmeer, Chemist and Biologist, who was involved in the nomination of the site for the 7 Most Endangered Programme, to hear about the Historic Centre of Stolberg’s inspiring journey.

It was a bad situation, the Historic Centre of Stolberg was badly flooded. It happened at an unexpected time. It was mid-July, and it had been raining for six weeks, when suddenly two meters of water flooded the main streets. It was dangerous and rough. This was a wakeup call, everyone’s talking about climate change and the effects and now we saw it. Two days later, the city centre was devastated.
